Subject: Throughput clarification & next steps after discovery call - BlueHarbor

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can size a tight Dedicated/Hosted recommendation:

Summary (what I heard)
- Primary use: conversational assistant and routing for warehouse ops and driver support.
- Typical request payloads are short instructions + context; average model output ~120 tokens.
- Traffic profile: steady background ~650 QPS (non-peak), with recurring 90s bursts up to ~6,800 QPS during shift change/dispatch windows.
- Streaming required for the mobile driver flow (progressive tokens to client) with soft-first-byte latency expectation.
- Target 95p latency for standard generation: <= 300 ms; streaming first-byte target: <= 150 ms.

Clarifying questions (helpful to confirm numbers or attach samples):
1) Can you confirm median tokens per request and a 95th percentile token count? Your shared CSV looked like avg=120 but some rows spike to 900.
2) For the burst windows — are those 90s spikes typical every hour, or more like 2x/day?
3) How many unique tenant keys / customer IDs map to the peak — is this many small callers or a handful of high-volume sources?
4) Any hard SLOs for tail latency beyond the ones on the call? (e.g., 99p target, SLA penalties)

Quick sizing note (back-of-envelope)
- If avg 120 tokens/request and peak 6,800 QPS, that maps to ~816k tokens/sec peak.
- With a modern LLM on GPU (int8), rough serving throughput assumptions vary a lot by model and sequence length; we should pick a model profile and run a microbenchmark.

Next steps I propose:
- Send a redacted traffic sample (CSV) for a 24hr window — if you can include timestamps, tokens per request, and client-id that helps our workload profiler.
- Aditya to schedule an ops-level deep-dive to confirm streaming semantics and instrumentation points.
- We'll return a Dedicated vs Hosted cost/latency trade table plus configuration (batching, KV cache warm strategies) within 48 business hours of receiving the sample.

Attaching our sizing template; recording from the call will be uploaded as well.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0162

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline and attached a small 24hr sample (blueharbor-traffic-sample.csv):

1) Token distribution: median ~110, mean ~135, 95th ~820 tokens, occasional spikes ~1,800 when full context + logs are included.
2) Burst cadence: the 90s spikes are tied to shift handovers and daily dispatch — they happen ~6 times/day (worst days), more typically 2–3 times/day.
3) Client distribution: ~75% of peak traffic comes from two large regional hubs (Oakland, Newark) + many smaller drivers creating the long tail.
4) SLA: Logistics ops require 95p <= 300ms for non-streaming; 99p is an internal goal but not contractual yet. Streaming first-byte <= 150ms is important for driver UX.

We attached the CSV and redacted client IDs. Let us know if you need more columns (payload sizes, region).

Thanks,
Sofia Marin
Head of Product — Driver Experience
BlueHarbor Logistics
sofia.marin@blueharbor.com

Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput clarification & next steps after discovery call - BlueHarbor

Sofia — great, that CSV is helpful. A few quick follow-ups from our side after skimming the sample:

Observations
- Token spikes to 1,800 are rare but significant for VM allocation; we should handle them via short-lived burst capacity rather than permanently overprovisioning.
- Given 75% of peak from two hubs, routing by region + warm KV cache for those hubs will drop cold-starts meaningfully.

Sizing sketch (more concrete)
- Using your 95th token count (820) and peak QPS 6,800: tokens/sec_peak = 6,800 * 820 ≈ 5.58M tokens/sec.
- That shifts the problem from QPS to token throughput for batching. Our runtime can process X tokens/sec per GPU for ModelProfile-A (we'll pick exact numbers after microbench).
- If we assume ModelProfile-A baseline of 300k tokens/sec per GPU (int8, streaming-friendly kernels), you'll need ~19 GPUs to get raw token throughput at peak; with smart batching + KV cache this could drop to ~12 GPUs effective.

Questions for sizing accuracy
- Are bursts uniform (all requests ~820 tokens) or mixed with many small requests + a few large ones? The mixed case favors batching effectiveness.
- Are driver sessions long-lived streams (single connection streaming many small outputs) or many short streams?

Action items
- Aditya: can you book a 60m tech-deep (ops + infra) tomorrow or Friday to validate streaming semantics and confirm which model profile to test.
- Sofia: if you can add a column for request_type (driver_chat vs routing_call) in the sample, that helps separate long streams from one-offs.
- Ben/Lauren: we'll produce a short Dedicated vs Hosted cost/latency sketch + a recommended burst policy (canary + autoscale buffer) within 48 hours after the tech-deep and microbench.

Thanks —
Ben
